allocation: Each sample's size is split equally over its decades in chronological order, the remainder going to the earliest decades; a decade with fewer eligible pages than its share gives all of them and the rest is split again among the others. Each decade's share is split over its titles the same way, in title-key order. Within a decade and title the pages with the lowest selection keys are taken, so each (decade, title) stratum is a simple random sample of its eligible pages and a page's design weight is the stratum's eligible count over its selected count.

audit.rule: The original 10% page audit (ocr/ja-ocr/quality.py sampled()): blake2b(doc_id, digest_size=8) read as a big-endian integer, mod 10,000, below the cut. audit_scored records whether the page is in that audit's page list.

exclusions.duplicate_image: the scan's sha256 equals that of an eligible page with a lower selection key
exclusions.mixed_language: the page-language decision is not one of the frame's decisions (a mixed page also carries another language)
exclusions.no_sidecar: no scan sidecar for the page in the scan fetcher's index: no cached image, so no image hash
exclusions.outside_era: dated outside the sample's declared decades
exclusions.scan_missing: the scan or its sidecar is not at its keep-set path, or the scan's size differs from the sidecar's
exclusions.sidecar_mismatch: the sidecar's doc_id, batch or batch version differs from the manifest row, its resolution is not the frame's, its format is not one of the frame's, or a JP2 sidecar has no md5 (the worker's own verification rule)

frame.description: Pages of the scan prefetch manifest pages-v20261010-2 (usnm-prefetch-manifest/1): every page of index pages-v20261010-2 whose damage v2 rate is at least 0.25. German, Danish, Finnish and Lithuanian pages are in its keep set, so their full-resolution scans stay cached on the scan host and the pilot needs no new image request. The frame is damaged pages only: a share measured on it is not the share of all German pages.

dan.rationale: The German question's period, ending in 1919, from the first decade with damaged Danish pages in the frame (the 1860s). The question for Danish, Finnish and Lithuanian is whether blackletter is used on our pages and how much a Fraktur model helps, not a precise prevalence. 100 pages per language keeps the three languages together at under a third of the German sample's reading. Were the 100 pages a simple random sample of the frame, a reader finding no blackletter would put the frame's share below about 3% at 95% (the rule of three), and a share near one half would be measured to about 10 points either way. They are not: equal decade and title shares give the pages unequal design weights, which widen both bounds, and an estimate for the frame must use the weights that summary.json records. This is a screening size, not a representative minimum, and estimates hold only for the damaged, cached frame.

fin.rationale: The German question's period, ending in 1919; damaged Finnish pages start in the 1900s. Most Finnish pages are from the 1920s and later, which this sample leaves out: they are outside the question's period, and a sample of them would be a separate declared draw. The size follows the Danish rationale: a screening size, not a representative minimum, whose unequal design weights make its bounds wider than those of a simple random sample of 100 pages.

ger.rationale: The issue's bounded task: about 1,000 German pages spanning each decade from 1850 to 1919. Equal decade allocation gives each decade the same number of pages, so a change of typeface over time can be seen: 143 pages would measure a share near one half to about 8 points either way at 95% as a simple random sample, and the equal title shares' unequal design weights widen that. Equal title allocation within a decade spreads the pages over as many titles as possible, because a paper's printer chose its typeface, not each page.

lit.rationale: The German question's period, ending in 1919; damaged Lithuanian pages start in the 1910s. The two 1940s Dirva pages (sn83035604) named on the issue are outside this era and are not a substitute for it. The size follows the Danish rationale: a screening size, not a representative minimum, whose unequal design weights make its bounds wider than those of a simple random sample of 100 pages.

selection: selection_key is the hex sha256 of seed + ':' + doc_id; a decade's titles are ordered by the hex sha256 of seed + ':title:' + lccn.
